subject: Biology
title: Predator–Prey Arms Races
description: A quick, practical guide to Predator–Prey Arms Races.

hook.text: Cheetahs evolved to run 110 km/h. Gazelles evolved to zigzag at 80 km/h. Neither can afford to lose.

buildup.text: Predators evolve better weapons. Prey evolve better defenses. It never stops.

discovery.text: Rough-skinned newts produce deadly tetrodotoxin. Garter snakes evolved resistance to eat them anyway.

twist.text: Each escalation by one side drives a counter-adaptation in the other—the Red Queen hypothesis.

climax.text: This endless competition is one of the most powerful engines of evolutionary change.

punchline.text: Run faster, bite harder, hide better. Or go extinct.

quiz.question: What is the Red Queen hypothesis?
options: Species must keep adapting just to survive against co-evolving rivals
Red coloring signals danger in nature

details.summary: Predator-prey arms races are ongoing evolutionary contests where each advance in one species drives a counter-adaptation in the other. Faster gazelles select for faster cheetahs, thicker shells select for stronger claws, and toxins select for venom resistance.
details.whyItMatters: Arms races are a primary engine of evolutionary change, driving increasing complexity and specialization. They demonstrate the Red Queen hypothesis: species must keep evolving just to maintain their relative fitness.
takeaways: Adaptations in predators drive counter-adaptations in prey and vice versa
The Red Queen hypothesis explains why evolution never reaches a final state
Arms races produce some of nature's most extreme adaptations

faq.question: What is the Red Queen hypothesis?
faq.answer: Named after the character in Alice in Wonderland who runs just to stay in place, it states that species must continually evolve to survive against co-evolving competitors and enemies. Standing still genetically means falling behind.

faq.question: What is the most extreme predator-prey arms race?
faq.answer: Rough-skinned newts and garter snakes may hold the record. Newts produce tetrodotoxin lethal enough to kill most predators. Resistant garter snakes evolved tolerance, driving newts to produce ever more potent toxin in an escalating molecular war.
